rows.post_text:
I give those short samples supporting weight.

Braves ML

Atlanta gets Acuña coming off a 5-for-9 start to this series and Murphy carrying a 1.308 OPS over the last 15 days.

I expect Ober to limit the traffic around Chicago’s dangerous swings sufficiently to make Minnesota’s chances worth the underdog payout.

Twins ML

Tonight’s White Sox nine is 11-for-58 this series.

My assumption is that Louisville’s changed offensive line can provide enough rushing room and protection for its returning backs to influence the whole game.

Louisville Cardinals +6.5

Isaac Brown averaged 8.8 yards per carry last season, and Keyjuan Brown averaged 7.3.

Detroit also preserved Jansen and Holton yesterday, so I give its bullpen a credible chance to keep this competitive.

Guardians ML

Smith, Gaddis and Sabrowski threw 18, 24 and 17 pitches Friday, respectively, and all avoided Saturday.

Colton Joseph is the main reason I want the points.

Wisconsin Badgers +21.5

CJ Carr threw 24 touchdown passes against six interceptions in 2025 and retains his connection with Jordan Faison.

My judgment is that Cincinnati’s best bats can make Harrison pay if that pitch remains hittable.

Reds ML

Harrison throws his four-seamer 57.4% of the time, and its whiff rate fell from 31% to 6% across his latest two starts.

My judgment is that Alvarez’s matchup and Washington’s opportunities against Wrobleski make the extra run and a half worth buying.

Nationals +1.5

House owns a .961 OPS against lefties in 82 at-bats, Crews .829 in 103, and Wood .841 in 165.

My judgment is that Texas can generate damaging contact here despite Seymour’s ability to collect strikeouts.

Rangers ML

Foscue has a 1.013 OPS against lefties and a .980 OPS over his last 15 days.

Arrighetti has allowed an .803 OPS to left-handed hitters versus .582 to right-handers.

Blue Jays ML

Caglianone’s .861 OPS against right-handed pitching makes his absence particularly relevant here.

Soto has a .767 OPS against lefties compared with 1.022 against righties; Lindor has .689 compared with .776.

Giants ML

Perdomo’s left-handedness also changes the matchup for the Mets.

Boston still needs to earn its advantage through the actual matchups.

Red Sox ML

Whitlock and Chapman rested Saturday after throwing 10 and 11 pitches Friday; Miller last worked Thursday.

Johnston and Moniak have substantially weaker supplied splits against left-handers, so that potential change matters directly to the case.

Rockies ML

The unresolved detail that could change my decision is St. Louis’ intended pitching sequence.

I expect Washington to exploit enough breakdowns in that coordination to sustain touchdown drives.

Washington Huskies -23.5

Williams threw 25 touchdowns against eight interceptions in 2025; his familiarity with the offense matters against a WSU defense returning no starters.

I give that potential finishing group more weight tonight than the nearly identical season bullpen ERAs.

Padres ML

Mason Miller, Adrian Morejon, Bradgley Rodriguez and Yuki Matsui all sat yesterday after throwing 22, 14, 9 and 12 pitches Friday.

I also expect Joyce and Natera to be usable in meaningful innings.

Angels +1.5

Joyce last threw 13 pitches on September 2, Natera threw 24 on September 4, and Watson needed only 6 yesterday.

I expect Lambert’s walks to bring Houston’s bullpen into this game early, and Arizona has the more workable relief options behind its starter.

Diamondbacks ML

Houston sits Diaz after his 4-for-7 series with a homer and starts Vázquez, whose OPS against lefties is .622.

I expect Chicago to get more innings from its starter and more opportunities against Miami’s middle relief.

Cubs ML

Holmes has allowed one run over his past four starts and 25 innings.

Seattle also has to convert opportunities; walks alone do not cover a run line.

Mariners -1.5

Jump allowed 2 earned runs with 9 strikeouts two starts ago, so an effective outing remains within his recent range.
